blocks.prompt: 11. If \(\frac{1}{a - c},\ \frac{1}{b - c},\ \frac{1}{b - a}\) are in A.P., then show that \(\frac{a - b}{a - c} = \frac{a - c}{b - a}\). [printed as 'the show']
blocks.explanation:
Yeh proof (saboot) wala sawal hai: di hui shart (A.P.) se shuru kar ke algebra se maangi hui baat tak pohanchna hai.
Teen numbers A.P. mein hon to beech wale ka dugna, baqi do ke jama ke barabar hota hai.
Plan: yeh shart likhna, fractions khatam karna, \(b - c\) ko \((b - a) + (a - c)\) likhna, simplify karna, aur aakhir mein divide.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(\frac{1}{a - c},\ \frac{1}{b - c},\ \frac{1}{b - a}\) A.P. mein hain.
Saabit karna hai: \(\frac{a - b}{a - c} = \frac{a - c}{b - a}\).
Tareeqa: \(2(\text{beech wali}) = \text{pehli} + \text{aakhri}\), phir algebra. Proof mein hum jawab ko maan kar nahi chalte; sirf di hui baat se aage barhte hain.

A.P. wali shart likhein
\[\dfrac{2}{b - c} = \dfrac{1}{a - c} + \dfrac{1}{b - a}\]
Kyun: \(x, y, z\) A.P. mein hon to \(y - x = z - y\), yani \(2y = x + z\). Yahan beech wali term \(\frac{1}{b - c}\) hai.

Right side ke fractions jama karein
\[= \dfrac{(b - a) + (a - c)}{(a - c)(b - a)}\]
\[= \dfrac{b - c}{(a - c)(b - a)}\]
Kyun: Fractions jama karne ke liye common denominator \((a - c)(b - a)\) liya. Upar \((b - a) + (a - c)\) mein \(-a\) aur \(+a\) cancel ho gaye aur \(b - c\) bacha.

Cross-multiply karein
\[2(a - c)(b - a) = (b - c)^2 \quad (1)\]
Kyun: Dono taraf \((b - c)(a - c)(b - a)\) se multiply kiya taake saare denominators khatam ho jayen. Left par \(2(a - c)(b - a)\) aur right par \((b - c)(b - c)\) bacha.

\((b - c)^2\) ko samajhdari se kholein
\[(b - c)^2 = [(b - a) + (a - c)]^2\]
\[= (b - a)^2 + 2(b - a)(a - c)\]
\[\quad + (a - c)^2\]
Kyun: Humein wohi brackets chahiye jo left side par hain: \((b - a)\) aur \((a - c)\). \(b - c = (b - a) + (a - c)\) sahi hai kyunke \(a\) cancel ho jata hai. Phir \((x + y)^2 = x^2 + 2xy + y^2\) lagaya.
Dhyan dein: \((b - c)^2\) ko \(b^2 - c^2\) likhna bohat aam ghalti hai; beech wali term \(2xy\) zaroor aati hai.

(1) mein rakh kar cancel karein
\[0 = (b - a)^2 + (a - c)^2\]
\[(b - a)^2 = -(a - c)^2\]
Kyun: \(2(a - c)(b - a)\) dono taraf mojood tha, dono se minus kiya to sirf squares bache.

Ek taraf ki shakal badlein
\[(b - a)(b - a) = -(a - c)^2\]
\[(a - b)(b - a) = (a - c)^2\]
Kyun: Minus ka nishan ek bracket ke andar le gaye: \(-(b - a) = a - b\). Ab dono taraf woh shakal hai jo humein chahiye.

\((a - c)(b - a)\) se divide karein
\[\dfrac{a - b}{a - c} = \dfrac{a - c}{b - a}\]
Kyun: \(a - c\) aur \(b - a\) zero nahi ho sakte, kyunke yeh di hui terms ke denominators hain. Divide karne se bilkul maangi hui baat aa gayi.

Real numbers ke baare mein ek baat
\[(b - a)^2 + (a - c)^2 = 0\]
Kyun: Real numbers mein do squares ka jama tabhi zero hota hai jab dono zero hon, yani \(a = b = c\); lekin phir di hui fractions ban hi nahi saktin. Matlab koi real \(a, b, c\) yeh shart poori nahi karte. Phir bhi proof algebra ke lehaaz se bilkul sahi hai (misaal: \(a = 0,\ b = i,\ c = 1\) dono baatein poori karte hain). Exam mein upar wala proof hi likhein.
blocks.final_answer: Saabit ho gaya: \(\frac{a - b}{a - c} = \frac{a - c}{b - a}\).

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab mein 'the show that' chhapa hai; durust 'then show that' hai. Yeh sirf chhapai ki ghalti hai, hisaab par koi asar nahi.
